title: Literature Review and Evidence Synthesis
answer: Evidence extraction, weighing the consensus, questions over your own sources, broad scans and translating between fields.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Evidence Extraction Tables
children.blurb: Evidence extraction tables are the structured grids in which a systematic review records what each included study reported, one row per study and one column per item of interest.

children.name: Weighing the Scientific Consensus
children.blurb: Weighing the scientific consensus means judging how strongly a body of research supports a claim, rather than treating a single paper or a single summary as decisive.

children.name: Questioning Your Own Sources
children.blurb: Questioning your own sources is the practice of testing the evidence a literature review rests on before that evidence is used to support a conclusion.

children.name: Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans
children.blurb: Deep research agents and landscape scans cover the use of AI systems to carry out multi step literature searches, gather sources, and assemble a structured view of what is known about a topic.

children.name: Translating Between Disciplines
children.blurb: Translating between disciplines is the work of moving a finding, method or term from the field that produced it into another field that can use it, without losing what it meant in the original.

sections.body: Literature review and evidence synthesis is the work of turning a pile of papers into a defensible account of what is known. In practice, AI systems now read full texts and pull out claims, methods, sample sizes and results into structured rows, which is why this site holds 14104 claims extracted from research works. They cluster findings by topic, flag where studies agree or conflict, and draft the first pass of a review that a person then checks. They also run broad scans across preprints and journals to surface work a keyword search would miss. The output is a map of the evidence, not a verdict, and the reading and judgement stay with the researcher.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Extraction is largely solved for clearly written papers with standard sections, and it fails quietly on tables, supplements, and ambiguous phrasing. Consensus weighing is useful when studies are numerous and comparable, and misleading when the field is small, divided, or dominated by one lab. Systems can now trace a claim back to the sentence it came from, which is why content here links to the original paper rather than to a search tool. What remains unsolved is judgement about quality, bias, and whether two studies are really measuring the same thing. Deep research agents produce fluent surveys that can cite plausible but wrong sources, so every reference needs opening. No automated pass replaces a careful reader, and none should be treated as settled fact.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Start with Evidence Extraction Tables when you need claims pulled from papers into something you can sort and count. Weighing the Scientific Consensus takes those rows and asks where the field actually agrees, which is the harder and more contested step. Questioning Your Own Sources is the counterweight, a check on whether the papers you gathered are the right ones and whether your search was fair. Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans covers the broad sweep, useful early when you do not yet know the shape of a field. Translating Between Disciplines sits at the end, for when the relevant work lives in another field under different words. Read together they form a loop, scan widely, extract carefully, weigh honestly, and question the whole set before you write.
